title: [3.13] gh-149449: Fix use-after-free in `_PyUnicode_GetNameCAPI` (GH-150323) (#150354)
consumer: Objects/obmalloc.c (the freed block's pool); see the C-model sibling
live_proof: measured on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc and ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0: REGRESSION-TEST-FAILS. Running the trigger is the proof.
fidelity: interpreter-trigger, real allocator. Upstream's own reproducer driven through the real CPython. The SAME defect also exists in ../pymalloc-repros as a C model consumer against the same allocator; that one locates the faulting instruction with a labelled probe and this one does not, so for attribution the C model is the stronger of the two. This one exists because the C models cannot be built for the cheribsd-revocation arm at all: shared/corpus.h's inline asm uses "r" constraints that cannot hold a 128-bit capability.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc on its lifetime port, CPY_SUBLET_MODE=1 (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completion while the block's arena stays live: pymalloc links the freed block onto its own pool free list, so the platform has no free to revoke. Once pymalloc returns an emptied arena to the system allocator (insert_to_freepool, when nf == ao->ntotalpools && ao->nextarena != NULL) the platform does have a free, and after a revocation sweep the stale access faults with SIGPROT si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG). Both outcomes are admissible; which one occurs depends on arena occupancy and sweep timing rather than on the defect, so this arm does not separate these cases. A bounds fault (si_code=1) would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=2 (not the mechanism) (spatial-20261007-020747); sublet DETECTED cause=24 (sublet-20261007-022142); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=5 (boundary-20261007-020413)
layer_note: unicodedata_create_capi (Modules/unicodedata.c:1465) takes the struct from PyMem_Malloc(sizeof(_PyUnicode_Name_CAPI)) = 16 bytes. The ASan nesting test cannot resolve this case because the fault is an indirect call through the dangling pointer -- ASan instruments loads and stores, not the jump, so it reports SEGV at the PC under PYTHONMALLOC unset and under PYTHONMALLOC=malloc alike. The routing was measured directly instead: PyMem_Malloc(16) freed and read back gives no ASan report with PYTHONMALLOC unset and heap-use-after-free with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, so the MEM domain is pymalloc and 16 bytes is under the 512-byte threshold. PyMem_RawMalloc(16) reports in both, which is the control.
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-use-after-free (READ 8) at PyCodec_NameReplaceErrors Python/codecs.c:968. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
